```python
def generate_palindrome():
    import random
    
    half_length = 128 # Half the length of the palindrome (to be doubled)
    
    # Generate a string of random lower case letters
    s = ''.join(random.choices('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz', k=half_length))
    
    # Reverse the string and concatenate it with the original
    return s + s[::-1]

print(generate_palindrome())
```

This code generates a 256-character long palindrome by generating a 128-character string of random lower case letters, reversing this string, and then concatenating the reversed string with the original. As such, it produces a palindrome that is at least 255 characters long. Please note that the generated palindrome might not be pronounceable or meaningful due to its random nature.

Also, the Python random library is used here which gives a uniform distribution over the possible outputs. It does not guarantee any statistical properties of being "random" in any formal sense.
